title: Tests in a linked worktree flock the source repo's live registry lock
description: A gate/pytest run inside a linked git worktree (~/Code/delegate-worktrees/...) held an exclusive flock on the SOURCE checkout's .delegate/.registry.lock for the length of the suite (observed: pytest pid 424049, cwd in the pgroup lane's worktree, fd 11uW on ~/Code/delegate-agent/.delegate/.registry.lock). Any registry-root resolution that walks to the git common dir escapes the worktree into the shared source workspace. Consequences observed 2026-08-26: a concurrent cursor run's _persist_final_progress timed out after 30s and crashed (see dlg registry-contention bead), and 'delegate worktree remove' timed out. Tests must never touch a registry outside their tmp_path — find the test/fixture that opens the real registry and pin registry resolution under test to the sandbox. Related: the 30s finalize timeout bead; this is the actual holder.
notes: PHASE0 (2026-08-27, W1-R lane b3b9473): escape NOT reproduced on current main — zero flock events on the source .delegate/.registry.lock across focused + full linked-worktree suite runs under real fcntl tracing (in-tree and subprocess-wide). Recharacterized: (a) deliverable is the watcher guardrail so any recurrence is caught attributed; (b) bounded investigation of the fd-inheritance hypothesis — flock is per open-file-description, so a child spawned (directly or via harness chain) while a lock fd is open+locked, with close_fds disabled or fd passing anywhere in the chain, holds the lock for its lifetime even after the parent closes; retirement/registration paths hold registry_lock while running subprocesses (worktree_mgmt.py:129). If the hypothesis proves out, fix is O_CLOEXEC/close_fds discipline at every spawn site reachable under a lock. Cost if wrong: guardrail still lands; znh stays open-dormant.
close_reason: Added independent linked-worktree source-lock watcher with subprocess coverage, fd-inheritance regression, and PHASE0-round2 clean audit; no causal escape reproduced.

title: Gate approval must certify the specific red it approved; a distinct red reusing the same gate key must re-park
description: From hq's Plan B production run (2026-08-27): a coordinator approval on a failure gate was treated as authorization to proceed even after a NEW, distinct red arose ('continue-approval-on-a-still-red-merge'). Engine-side, approval is already gate-key-scoped (record_approval/approval_allows/_latest_unapproved_gate_event), so a new gate KEY re-parks correctly. The hazard is when a DISTINCT red reuses the SAME gate key (gate key derived from stable gate identity rather than the failing result) — then the first red's approval wrongly covers the second. This is the gate-side analog of the reject() sequenced-invalidation bug (Cursor F2/F6). Fix options: (a) fold the result/attempt into the gate key so a new red = new key requiring fresh approval; or (b) record which result-hypothesis the approval approved and re-park when the current red differs. G-compat: must be additive (v1 gate keys byte-preserved; the paused deck-parity run's approved keys stay valid). Wave-3-adjacent engine follow-up; not in the current r3 graph.

(1) LOCKS: close gates stall admission — process_item runs a close stage inside SPINE_LOCK for the whole agent run, and a wave-level failure gate from the close settle path holds MERGE_LOCK while close_gate_and_wait drains every in-flight agent, freezing all integration for hours behind one failed close verifier; fix direction from the run: release MERGE_LOCK before raising a wave-level gate. (2) MERGE-BASE: contribution diffs computed against a single merge-base misattribute files when a lane branched off a since-reset merge commit — the reset leaves descendants poisoned (DP.42). (3) COORDINATOR_TASKS: the adjudicator marks fix tasks coordinator-owned but the engine hands every fix task to a lane (DP.1 rounds 3-5: lane re-applied plan edits, integrator hit conflicts on all seven doc paths) — decide whether the workflow contract grows a coordinator-task channel (parks for coordinator action instead of spawning) or planc reroutes. Anything determined planc-side bounces back to hq with the trace.
close_reason: Bounced to hq per Sol r2 finding 10 + hq confirmation in #v2-hardening: SPINE_LOCK/MERGE_LOCK, contribution merge-base, and coordinator-task ownership are all generated-workflow/planc concepts — delegate exposes only generic DSL primitives, no merge-lock or coordinator-task model. hq's committed adjudication (writing-plans ADJUDICATION-r1.md rulings 6/9/10) disposes of all three; hq confirmed no new engine primitive needed.

title: Durable slot release / named-scope dynamic admission for parked workflow items
description: Wave-3, design-first. wp-2m8.42 verbatim: the per-item scheduler uses one stable pipeline scope; a parked item retains its pipeline slot because the runtime exposes no future/completion callback or public slot release, so with itemThreads below active+parked count an unrelated ready item waits. Deck run survived only because 42 items < 64 default threads. Add a durable named-scope admission primitive or safe item-slot release WITHOUT changing replay keys (G-compat constraint: the paused deck-parity run must still resume). Acceptance from the bead: park an item, release its slot, admit an unrelated ready item, later resume the parked item under the same replay-stable structural scope.

title: Usage errors exit zero; verify landed observability fixes carry regression tests; spawn-burst residual
description: Wave-3. OPEN: pc2_447115752c82e925 — delegate prints misplaced_global_option and exits 0, so a backgrounded launch reads as success while nothing ran; usage errors must exit non-zero (do not conflate with pc2_64709327952c0506, the flag-placement policy question). VERIFY-ON-MAIN (already healed, confirm regression coverage): f627faf IN main (agent_timeout rows carry key/label/model; workflow run --notify fires on paused/failed/succeeded), 0c62e4e IN main (failed tracked run payload carries stderrTail; EPIPE warning names child exit + stderr). RESIDUAL: burst-launching ~12 lanes still hits launcher pool exhaustion (3 died at 0s, Broken pipe) — now visible instead of hidden; retry-on-EPIPE was explicitly rejected as unworkable; decide whether delegate serializes/staggers child spawn under burst or documents the stagger. Report healed SHAs to hq for their papercut closes.
notes: SPLIT per Sol r2 F10 before W3 launch: (a) usage-errors-exit-nonzero = the implementation item; (b) f627faf/0c62e4e = verify-only regression receipts; (c) launcher burst-capacity = policy decision for Trey, not lane work.

title: StructuredOutput tolerance: accept JSON-string payloads; schema-fail parks carry the parsed report
description: Wave-3. (1) The claude engine hands StructuredOutput a JSON string on large payloads and the tool layer rejects it (DP.23, 23:37Z: complete 8-task adjudication in the completion report, StructuredOutput failed all four attempts with value-must-be-object x3) — accept a string that decodes to the schema. (2) When a report parses but fails schema validation, park WITH the parsed report attached, not an empty payload (DP.12, 22:00Z: retry lane had succeeded with 8 commits, park showed empty result, fix was obvious from the report and invisible from the park) — contract D. Also VERIFY-ON-MAIN: wp-2m8.34's two sub-bugs (codex preflight rejecting non-strict schemas pre-launch; parse_json_tolerant picking decoy brackets) claim fixed per the bead's own notes — repro-on-base, add regression tests if missing, report healed SHA to hq in #v2-hardening so wp-2m8.34 can close.

title: Lane health heuristics: zero-commit flag, stalled-stream kill, structured-retry pool roll
description: Wave-3 design bead. From deck-parity run observations: (1) a lane with zero commits at half its stage budget should be flagged (DP.16: 60 min, 7MB read-only output, zero commits); (2) a lane with zero tool calls and a stalled non-thinking stream for N minutes should be killed early, not run out its full timeout (DP.17: omp gemini lane emitted only backtick fences for 25 min); (3) a structured retry should route to the NEXT pool entry, not re-run the model that just failed structurally. Design-first: these are policy knobs on the workflow runtime; defaults must not surprise existing workflows.
notes: NARROWED per Sol r2 F10: the zero-tool-call/stalled-stream kill already shipped — stall_watchdog.py wired at runner.py:1852-1865/2048-2064, tests test_stall_watchdog.py; healed SHAs fa408af + 1b1dbbf (reported to hq). Residual scope: zero-commits-at-half-budget flag + structured-retry pool-roll only.

title: Registry finalization lock contention: concurrent lanes crash _persist_final_progress
description: With 4 concurrent lanes registered in one source workspace, a cursor safe run's finalization timed out on .delegate/.registry.lock after 30.0s and crashed with TimeoutError in _persist_final_progress (runner.py:614 via _finalize_tracked_run). The child had completed its work; the run was left marked 'stale' and the CLI exited 1, so a successful review read as a failed launch. Finalization should retry/backoff well past 30s or persist a fallback record outside the lock; a completed child's output must never be reported as failure because of registry contention. Observed 2026-08-26, ship-cleanup fleet.
close_reason: Implemented configurable registry-lock budgets, atomic per-run finalize WAL fallback/replay with cancel precedence, launch pre-spawn contention failure, and regression coverage in commits 1eeada5 and 7ad0c85.

comments.author: Trey Goff
comments.text: REGISTRY_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is hardcoded 30.0 in run_registry.py:64 — no env/config override. Third occurrence in one session: a launch-side registration also died on the same lock (cursor re-verify lane, 2026-08-26). Fix should include a configurable/env timeout plus launch- and finalize-side resilience.

description: Inventory repo-supported Delegate harnesses, safely update local CLIs, review current primary documentation, implement only required compatibility changes, complete native and Claude review gates, validate, and open a draft PR only for meaningful green changes.

title: capabilities refresh misreports fingerprint_mismatch as requested_harnesses_not_installed
description:
resolve_harness_selector returns fingerprint_mismatch (harness_discovery.py) when the configured binary answers as a different known harness. That collapses to installed: false, so `capabilities refresh`/`setup` tell the user the harness is missing when it is actually present and running under the wrong identity. Confirmed still true against current code: capability_commands.py's requested_harnesses_not_installed path only checks record.get("installed") is True, with no separate branch for fingerprint_mismatch, even though a probeStatus field now exists in the schema (capability_commands.py, describe_payload.py, model_discovery.py).

The honest fix needs probeStatus as a closed, schema-validated enum ({ok, partial, missing, error}) persisted in the cache, distinguishing "wrong harness" from "missing" — design-first, not a quick wording change. Precedent: the CONFIGURED_SELECTOR_MISSING vs probe_missing split already in harness_discovery.py.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record).
close_reason: Implemented typed fingerprint-mismatch provenance through SelectorResolution, refresh attempts, and CLI diagnostics; real CLI proof is tests.test_capability_commands.CapabilityCommandTests.test_real_cli_refresh_surfaces_typed_identity_mismatch; commit 2923ba3.

title: Discovery cache keyed on auth profile can ping-pong across invocation contexts
description:
An agent sandbox resolves e.g. `codex` to a cmux shim under TMPDIR; a login shell resolves the same auth profile to /opt/homebrew/bin/codex. Same profile, two answers, one cache file, so two contexts can each invalidate the other's record and ping-pong indefinitely. Masked today because drift comparison uses configured selectors rather than resolved paths, but any future move toward resolved-path comparison walks straight into it. Not yet designed.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record).
close_reason: Reproduced base PATH/TMPDIR ping-pong, added bounded context-keyed cache migration plus serialized merge writes; real CLI proof is tests.test_capability_commands.CapabilityCommandTests.test_real_cli_context_refreshes_do_not_mutually_invalidate; commits 2923ba3 and 0bd5947.

title: Flaky: test_structured_retry_timeout_exhaustion_reaps_every_workspace races 0.2s timeout vs 1s fake-harness sleep under load
description: tests/test_workflow_commands.py::test_structured_retry_timeout_exhaustion_reaps_every_workspace uses a real fake-codex subprocess with FAKE_CODEX_SLEEP_SECONDS=1 against timeout=0.2; under system load the timing race can flake (observed 1 spurious fail then 8/8 pass, 2026-08-27, right after a lane finished). Same class as the index.json rename-race flake. Not a logic bug — the W2 N-D interaction logic fix (8dd10c6) is verified 8/8. Durable fix: make the timing margin robust (larger sleep/timeout separation) or gate the real-subprocess timing tests behind a serialized marker so they don't race under xdist load. Low priority; causes occasional spurious gate reds.

title: Flaky: test_silent_running_harness_snapshots_as_running races atomic rename under parallel gate load
description: tests/test_end_to_end_tracking.py::EndToEndTrackingTests::test_silent_running_harness_snapshots_as_running fails intermittently under the full parallel gate with 'BoundedReadError: record file has 0 links' on .delegate/index.json (private_io.py:57). Passes 5/5 in isolation; failed 1x under full gate load 2026-08-27. Pre-existing (Wave-1 did not touch the test or the 0-links guard). Root cause: the bounded read of index.json races the harness subprocess's atomic rename — the reader holds the old inode open when rename unlinks it, so st_nlink==0. Durable fix: make the bounded reader retry once on st_nlink==0 (the rename is atomic, so a re-open gets the new inode) rather than raising, OR have the test synchronize on the write. Not a blocker for Wave-1 ship (unrelated pre-existing flake).

title: creationContext records the synced dirty-path list, not just a count
description: Wave-3, small. wp-2m8.16 (relocated here per its own text): audit counters cannot subtract launch-workspace dirt synced into a worktree because the manifest records only a count. Record the path list (bounded; cap + overflow marker if huge). Cross-links dlg-44w.4's dirty-verdict work — the same list lets the dirty verdict subtract spine-synced untracked files.
notes: NARROWED per Sol r2 F10: premise false — syncedFileDigests already records every seeded path (worktree_records.py:29,67-103; worktree_execution.py:551-562), retirement consumes it (worktree_mgmt.py:88-110). Residual: bounded public projection in creationContext if the consumer still wants it; else close healed-by-existing-machinery.

title: OMP behavior probe test picks wrong binary and deny tests pass vacuously on a dead lane
description: tests/test_omp_read_only_behavior.py resolves shutil.which('omp') which on the estate is the raw unbrokered binary (~/.local/bin/omp, default model fireworks/kimi-k2.7-code, invalid key -> instant 401), not estate-omp. The deny tests assert a file does NOT exist, so a lane that errors instantly passes them vacuously — observed 2026-08-27: full suite 'passed' the two deny tests in 2.4s against a dead binary; only the read test caught it. Also the omp default model (zai-glm-4.7) is archived, so even estate-omp needs an explicit --model. Fix: env override for the binary (e.g. DELEGATE_OMP_BEHAVIOR_BIN) + explicit model arg + guard deny tests against vacuity (require the same run's read probe to succeed, or assert turn_end stopReason != error before trusting a deny).
close_reason: Added binary/model overrides and non-vacuous OMP transcript guard with unit coverage; checkpoint e917c15.

title: Test gaps from followup-r2 re-verify: retire_completed_worktree reconstruction + e2e followup-after-schema-retry
description: Cursor re-verify (2026-08-26, verdict MERGE) confirmed both MAJOR fixes but flagged two coverage gaps: (1) worktree_mgmt.retire_completed_worktree's manifest-reconstruction path has no direct test; (2) no end-to-end test of followup() after a schema retry in a persistent worktree (the attach path is only code-traced). Also noted: KeyboardInterrupt during parse after a child returns can skip the supervisor's worktree-hold release (leak-to-reap, acceptable per dlg-3w5 rulings but worth a regression note when reap ships).
close_reason: Added real manifest-reconstruction matrix and persistent-worktree followup-after-schema-retry e2e; checkpoint b82968c.

title: Mail tests break in shallow checkouts: tempdir at parents[3] of test file
description: tests/test_mail_*.py setUp creates its TemporaryDirectory at Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] — two levels above the repo root, deliberately outside the tree. In a checkout at depth 2 (e.g. a git worktree at /tmp/x) that resolves to / and every test fails with PermissionError, 30 failures that look environmental. Deep checkouts silently drop temp dirs into unrelated parent directories instead. Fix: walk up from the repo root to the first writable directory, or use a dedicated env-var override with a tmpfile fallback that is still outside the repo.
close_reason: Shared validated mail tempdir helper plus shallow-worktree subprocess proof; checkpoint e917c15.

title: Expose effective isolation backend in terminal JSON
description:
## Problem
Terminal run JSON omits the effective copy/bwrap sandbox backend even though the manifest records it; expose and document the backend in the top-level contract.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run Delegate with --json and compare the terminal object with the run manifest isolation.backend field.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal JSON includes the effective isolation backend for run results, documentation and tests describe the field, and existing manifest behavior remains intact.

title: Remove droid, opencode, kimi engines from delegate
description: RESCOPED per Trey 2026-08-27 (original filing misread the 2026-08-18 ruling): do NOT excise engine code from source. Remove the droid, opencode, and kimi lanes/models from the INSTALLED RUNTIME configuration only (~/.delegate live config), so 'delegate models' stops offering them; OMP carries those model families (kimi->kimi-code/k3, ox->openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha, etc.). Engine source code, parsers, and tests stay. Coordinator-direct task, no lane needed.

Removed the opencode stanza (ox -> opencode/x-preview-f-free) from ~/.delegate/config.json and config.personal.json (backups: *.bak-dlg0lk); droid and kimi had no configured models to remove. title: Design and ship explicit worktree reap deletion verb
description:
`worktree gc --all` (shipped v0.21.0) only scans and reports orphaned worktrees whose source repo is gone — it deletes nothing, at any depth, by design. The actual reclamation verb was deliberately deferred: a separate explicit `worktree reap --older-than DAYS --yes` command with real pool-root validation. This is the lesson from the round-1 review blocker on the original sweep: `--pool PATH` (arbitrary user root) composed with empty-dir rmdir meant `gc --pool "$HOME"` could have removed home directories — each piece was safe alone, so the deletion verb needs its own careful design pass, not a flag bolted onto gc.

Related caveats to fold into this design rather than opening separate tickets (per the deferred doc's own instruction): source_root_missing records are permanently visible/unclearable since deletion depends on a live source that creation didn't require; and `_has_detached_backlink` can mislabel a non-worktree directory nested under an unrelated ancestor repo — cosmetic today, becomes load-bearing once a reaper acts on classification.

Source: docs/plans/deferred.md, "Still open after the sweep" (2026-07-25 sweep record) + worktree gc fixes #3/#4 section (v0.18.0).

comments.author: Trey Goff
comments.text: Ruling (2026-08-26, ship-cleanup run): completion-time retirement (dlg-7te fix 1) deliberately retires only via the owner run's record — attached resume runs that clean a previously retained tree do not retire it. Orphan/retained-tree reclamation is this bead's scope (reap verb). Cost if wrong: retained-but-now-clean trees accumulate until reap ships.

comments.author: Trey Goff
comments.text: Ruling 2 (2026-08-26): worktrees of resumable=True runs are RETAINED at completion (reason resumable_session) — --resumable is an explicit opt-in to re-entry, so retiring the tree would break the followup contract. These retained trees are additional inventory for this reap verb. Cost if wrong: resumable-heavy workloads re-accumulate worktrees until reap ships.
